topic: Sharp shared-SCM bounds for trajectory-conditioned Shapley credit in a finite-horizon finite-state/action Markov SCM: characterize attained coordinate intervals under arbitrary within-time potential-next-state coupling, one coupling shared across coalition worlds, exact coalition compression and constrained-width endpoint compilation, an open-family gap from independent coalition optimization, and simultaneous confidence-fiber inference for the φ-PPO consumer without claiming sharp PTR RMS priorities.

open_problems.open_problem: For each Li–Lee–Bareinboim trajectory-conditioned Shapley coordinate, characterize the attained sharp interval over finite Markov SCMs with fixed transition marginals and arbitrary within-time response-table coupling when one posterior coupling is shared by every coalition world, and prove a persistent strict gap from coalitionwise optimization.

source_refs.venue: Reinforcement Learning Conference / Reinforcement Learning Journal

open_problems.why_unsolved: The attribution papers either select a counterfactually independent SCM or optimize a generic static L3-Shapley functional. Lally et al. supply the row-gluing substrate, yet a signed Shapley average reuses the same latent response rows along every coalition path, so separately sharp coalition values need not coexist in one SCM. The failed DTE proposal records the analogous compatibility failure and shows why a local-feasibility-to-global-pasting step cannot be asserted. The destination still needs an exact posterior projection for the sequential objective, compatible endpoint witnesses, and a normalized separation argument showing that the common-SCM restriction is strictly active on an open family rather than at one fragile numerical instance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact finite posterior response-row program for each coordinate, proofs of compact attainment and constructive endpoint SCMs, and a rational two-step family with closed shared and independently optimized intervals whose strictly positive gap persists on a neighborhood.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact destination estimand, skill-versus-luck motivation, policy-switching semantics, and φ-PPO consumer framing to preserve while weakening the coupling assumption.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Delayed stochastic rewards obscure causal action credit -> trajectory-conditioned counterfactual Shapley values separate action from luck -> their numerical value depends on a cross-world coupling not fixed by transition marginals -> shared-SCM sharp intervals state exactly what is identified.

method_exemplars.technique: Parameterize transition response tables and prove by simultaneous row gluing that locally feasible posterior rows extend to one exogenous distribution with all required marginals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Endpoint SCMs need exactly this common-law construction, with a global signed trajectory-Shapley objective replacing a single transition-coordinate objective.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce arbitrary finite discrete SCMs to canonical response types and optimize the resulting polynomial counterfactual functional with constructive sharpness witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It licenses finite response-type optimization as an exact search over compatible SCMs and is the generic audit baseline for the proposed row-compressed program.

method_exemplars.technique: Pair a sharp dynamic bound characterization with orthogonal endpoint estimators, semiparametric efficiency calculations, and asymptotic normality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how a sharp dynamic causal endpoint can support a genuine estimator-and-limit-law rung rather than treating inference after optimization as automatic.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the shared-SCM trajectory-Shapley endpoint program be compiled into an exact mixed-elimination algorithm that compresses the 2^H coalition sum to polynomial size, is exponential only in a formally defined constrained width, and retains one optimizing row assignment for all coalition and state realizations?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Expectation over state paths, the Shapley coalition average, and maximization over response rows are noncommuting operations. Eliminating max variables too early lets the SCM depend on an unobserved state or coalition; duplicating a row variable across factors silently returns the independent-coalition outer bound. Exact do-Shapley compression does not include posterior conditioning or a common latent optimizer, while marginal-MAP theory rules out an ordinary-treewidth slogan. The prior complete-calculus run encountered the same local-to-global obstruction: locally chosen atoms did not automatically form one compatible global law. The missing object is therefore an optimization-preserving invariant with explicit factor scopes, legal orders, bit accounting, and optimizer backtracking.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A polynomial-size factor or arithmetic-circuit representation, a proved sum-before-max elimination invariant, an explicit constrained width w and O(H² N d^(w+1)) arithmetic bound, and backpointers whose recovered shared row assignment compiles to an endpoint SCM and matches exhaustive enumeration.

writing_exemplar.why: Its tractability section begins from the same exponential coalition formula in the exact sequential credit-assignment setting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact trajectory Shapley credit averages exponentially many policy-switching worlds -> stochastic sampling is practical for one selected SCM -> partial identification adds one optimizer shared across every world -> exact endpoints require coalition compression plus legal mixed elimination.

method_exemplars.technique: Partition interventions into structural equivalence classes and aggregate their Shapley weights instead of evaluating every coalition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination needs an exact quotient of the coalition lattice, augmented with Markov trajectory and shared posterior-row state.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent mixed marginalization and maximization explicitly, then prove validity only for elimination schedules respecting operator noncommutativity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The compiler's central proof obligation is the same: preserve one maximizer through all chance and coalition summations.

method_exemplars.technique: Transform and prune smooth decomposable circuits with certified solution-preserving splits and recover an exact marginal-MAP optimizer.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is a concrete compiler template that returns an optimizer certificate while exploiting circuit structure rather than merely asserting a recurrence.

open_problems.open_problem: From multinomial transition samples, can simultaneous confidence-fiber inversion cover the entire vector of shared-SCM trajectory-Shapley identified intervals and yield endpoint consistency controlled by the smallest factual transition probability rather than the full trajectory probability?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cellwise intervals or coordinatewise endpoint intervals do not imply simultaneous containment of the vector identified set. The endpoint is a nonsmooth optimization map whose active row faces can switch, so naive endpoint bootstrap arguments are invalid at ties. Factual conditioning also divides by observed transition-cell probabilities; approaching zero changes the posterior feasible set discontinuously unless a closure is specified and prevents uniform consistency without positivity. Lally et al. explicitly leave sampling uncertainty open, and the accepted partial-transport run shows that even a finite polyhedral endpoint needs a dedicated face-aware or conservative whole-set argument. The sequential setting must additionally prove that sensitivity accumulates locally across time, rather than through the exponentially smaller full-trajectory probability.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A simultaneous multinomial row confidence set whose exact fiber image covers every coordinate interval on one event, plus a uniform endpoint or Hausdorff consistency theorem on κ-positive factual cells with an explicit O(DHδ/κ) perturbation modulus and a stated zero-evidence closure rule.

writing_exemplar.why: Its conclusion states the direct known-transition to data-estimated-transition gap in the closest compatible-SCM MDP setting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Compatible-SCM bounds protect against structural uncertainty -> existing formulas take transition marginals as known -> empirical transitions add sampling uncertainty before endpoint optimization -> confidence-fiber projection must protect the whole Shapley identified set.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert calibrated sample restrictions and obtain projection endpoints by re-optimizing over a confidence-feasible parameter set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Transition marginals are nuisance parameters in exactly such a confidence fiber, which must then be projected through the shared-SCM endpoint program.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct simultaneous multinomial proportion intervals with an exactly computed fixed-sample confidence coefficient.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each finite MDP transition row is multinomial, so these regions give a direct finite-sample substrate for the joint transition-law fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the directional derivative of a nondifferentiable functional and resample that derivative instead of naively bootstrapping the plug-in map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sharp endpoints are minima and maxima of a parameterized program and kink when endpoint SCM faces switch.

literature_map:
Li, Lee, and Bareinboim (2026, RLC/RLJ, arXiv:2607.16999) define trajectory-conditioned φ-values, use a 2^H coalition kernel, and select counterfactually independent response rows.
Lee, Plecko, and Bareinboim (2026, Technical Report R-135) establish generic nonidentification and tight SCM-optimization bounds for counterfactual Shapley values, so novelty must lie in shared sequential structure and compilation.
Lally, Kazemi, and Paoletti (2026, AAMAS, arXiv:2502.13731) give tight counterfactual transition bounds and simultaneous row gluing, but not a signed multi-policy Shapley endpoint.
Their known-transition analysis explicitly leaves data-estimated transition probabilities and confidence intervals open.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, ICML, arXiv:2110.05690) provide the finite canonical-SCM and polynomial-program foundation for attained sharp discrete counterfactual bounds.
Duarte et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2109.13471) automate sharp discrete causal bounds, while Zaffalon et al. (2024, IJAR, DOI 10.1016/j.ijar.2023.109111) expose credal-network structure and NP-hardness even on polytrees.
Balke and Pearl (1994, UAI) are the foundational response-function/linear-program anchor; Oberst and Sontag (2019, ICML) illustrate the alternative point-selecting Gumbel-Max SCM for counterfactual MDPs.
Witter et al. (2026, ICML, arXiv:2602.07203) compress exact do-Shapley by irreducible intervention classes, but do not handle factual posterior worlds or one shared latent optimizer.
Liu and Ihler (2013, JMLR, arXiv:1302.6584) and Park and Darwiche (2004, JAIR, DOI 10.1613/jair.1236) show why mixed sum/max elimination needs constrained orders.
Choi, Friedman, and Van den Broeck (2022, AISTATS, arXiv:2111.04833) give an exact marginal-MAP compiler pattern with solution-preserving circuit transformations and optimizer recovery.
Wiesemann, Kuhn, and Rustem (2013, Mathematics of Operations Research) and later nonrectangular robust-MDP work distinguish one common adversarial kernel from rowwise reoptimization.
Bennett et al. (2024, NeurIPS, arXiv:2404.00099) pair sharp dynamic value bounds with efficient asymptotically normal endpoint estimation.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica), Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud), and Wang (2008, JMVA) supply calibrated projection, nonsmooth directional inference, and simultaneous multinomial confidence machinery.
Targeted searches found no paper jointly handling trajectory-conditioned Shapley credit, arbitrary within-time row coupling, one SCM shared across every coalition, exact width-controlled elimination, and whole-set multinomial fiber inversion.
